parts.text: Which claim correctly gives its perimeter?

options.text: Perimeter $= 4 \times 9 = 36\,\mathrm{m}$, because all four sides are equal.
Perimeter $= 3 \times 9 = 27\,\mathrm{m}$, treating the courtyard as an equilateral triangle.
Perimeter $= 9\,\mathrm{m}$, taking the printed side length as the perimeter.
Perimeter $= 4 \times 9 = 36\,\mathrm{m}$ even if the four sides were unequal.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Bhavna's square courtyard has each side $9\,\mathrm{m}$ long.

part_answers.answer: A square has four equal sides, so its perimeter is $4\times 9=36\,\mathrm{m}$.

teacher.key_rationale: Four equal sides of 9 m give perimeter 36 m. Using 3 sides swaps the polygon; using one side alone or dropping equal-side condition is wrong.
